stem: A shop in Kisumu wants to store thousands of product photos and videos so customers can view them in a web browser. Which Azure Storage service fits best?
why_correct: Blob storage is designed for large amounts of unstructured data such as images and video, and it can serve them straight to a browser.
why_a_wrong: Queues hold messages passed between parts of an application; they are not for storing media files.
why_c_wrong: Tables store structured NoSQL data and are not meant for photos or videos.
why_d_wrong: Disks are block storage volumes attached to Azure virtual machines; they are not used to serve media to browsers.
author: yego

stem: A SACCO wants to keep scanned loan records for several years. The files are almost never opened, and staff can wait for retrieval when they are needed. Which blob access tier gives the lowest storage cost?
why_correct: The Archive tier is meant for data that is rarely accessed, kept for at least 180 days and can tolerate slow retrieval. It has the lowest storage cost of the tiers.
why_a_wrong: Hot is meant for data that is accessed often, so it is a poor fit for records that are rarely opened.
why_b_wrong: Cool is for infrequently accessed data kept at least 30 days, but its storage cost is higher than Archive.
why_d_wrong: Cold is for infrequently accessed data kept at least 90 days, but Archive is the tier built for the rarest access and has the lowest storage cost.
author: yego

stem: A bank in Nairobi wants storage that keeps copies in three availability zones in its main region and also copies the data to a second region using LRS. Which redundancy option does this?
why_correct: GZRS uses ZRS in the primary region, so the data sits across three availability zones, and then copies it to a secondary region using LRS.
why_a_wrong: LRS keeps three copies within a single datacenter in the primary region, with no zones and no second region.
why_b_wrong: ZRS spreads copies across three availability zones, but only within the primary region, so nothing goes to a second region.
why_c_wrong: GRS uses LRS in the primary region, so it does not spread across availability zones there, then copies to a secondary region.
author: yego

objective_text: Describe storage account options and storage types
stem: A company needs a storage account that holds only file shares and supports both SMB and NFS. Which storage account type should it choose?
why_correct: The premium file shares account type is built for Azure Files only, and it is the one to use when you need both SMB and NFS file shares.
why_b_wrong: Premium page blobs holds page blobs only, so it cannot host file shares.
why_c_wrong: Premium block blobs is for block and append blobs, not file shares.
why_d_wrong: Standard general-purpose v2 does cover Azure Files, but for NFS support the page points to the premium file shares account type.
author: yego

objective_text: Identify options for moving files, including AzCopy, Azure Storage Explorer, and Azure File Sync
stem: A company has a local Windows file server and wants its files to stay automatically synced, in both directions, with Azure Files. Which tool should it use?
why_correct: Azure File Sync is installed on the local Windows server and keeps it bi-directionally synced with the files in Azure Files.
why_a_wrong: AzCopy is a command-line tool, and its sync works in one direction only.
why_b_wrong: Azure Storage Explorer is a graphical app for managing files and blobs, not a service that keeps a server synced.
why_c_wrong: Azure Data Box is a physical device for moving large amounts of data, not an ongoing sync tool.
author: yego

objective_text: Describe migration options, including Azure Migrate and Azure Data Box
stem: A company wants to move a large one-time batch of on-premises data to Azure using a physical storage device that Microsoft ships to its office. Which service fits?
why_correct: Azure Data Box is a physical migration service. Microsoft ships a storage device, which you fill with data and send back, so no network transfer is needed.
why_a_wrong: Azure Migrate is used to assess and migrate on-premises infrastructure online, so it does not ship a physical device.
why_c_wrong: AzCopy is a command-line tool that copies data to and from storage accounts, so it does not use a shipped device.
why_d_wrong: Azure File Sync keeps a local Windows file server synced with Azure Files, so it is not a bulk-shipping service.
author: yego
